chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, evil manners spoil the deed just as vinegar spoils honey.

key_terms.الْعَمَلَ: The deed/work (often referring to acts of worship or righteous actions)

ai.seo_question: How does bad character affect the validity of good deeds in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), transmitted through the chain of al-Kulayni’s *al-Kafi*, the Imam employs the vivid metaphor of vinegar spoiling honey to illustrate how *su' al-khuluq* (bad character) corrupts the spiritual integrity of otherwise valid deeds. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on *khuluq* not merely as social etiquette, but as a fundamental determinant of the acceptance (*qabul*) of worship, ensuring that outward acts are matched by inner moral purity. The comparison underscores that just as a small amount of vinegar ruins the sweetness of honey, a dominant trait of ill-temper can nullify the reward of extensive religious practice.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The evil mannerism is a spoiler of the deed just as the vinegar spoils the honey’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘
Wickedness and evil behavior destroys and spoils good deeds just as vinegar spoils honey.’”
